classification.difficultyReason: Translate two familiar fractional constraints into simultaneous equations and eliminate.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming a pair of simultaneous equations.

Four times Brian’s age exceeds Andrew’s age by 20 years and one-third of Andrew’s age is less than Brian’s age by two years. Find their ages.

answer.short: Andrew is 36 years old and Brian is 14 years old.
answer.worked:
Let $a$ be Andrew’s age in years and $b$ be Brian’s age in years.
$$\begin{align*}4b-a&=20 &&\text{(1)}\\b-\frac{a}{3}&=2 &&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$
Multiply equation (2) by 3:
$$\begin{align*}3b-a&=6 &&\text{(3)}\end{align*}$$
Subtract equation (3) from equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}(4b-a)-(3b-a)&=20-6\\b&=14\end{align*}$$
Substitute into equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}4\times14-a&=20\\56-a&=20\\a&=36\end{align*}$$
Check: $4\times14-36=20$ and $14-\frac{36}{3}=2$.

Andrew is 36 years old and Brian is 14 years old.
